title: GraphRAG: The Marriage of Knowledge Graphs and RAG: Emil Eifrem
talk_summary: Emil Eifrem argues that GraphRAG — using a knowledge graph on the retrieval path, seeded by vector search and expanded by graph traversal — improves answer accuracy and makes RAG systems more debuggable and explainable. He cites research showing 3x and ~75% accuracy gains, and demos a tool that auto-builds a graph from PDFs, YouTube and Wikipedia.

takeaways.technique: Graph-expanded retrieval instead of flat top-K chunks
takeaways.what_they_do: Use vector search as a 'primary key' lookup into a graph, then traverse relationships to pull in adjacent context (related products, authors, hierarchy) before ranking and passing to the LLM.

takeaways.technique: Explicit graph as a debugging/audit surface
takeaways.what_they_do: Because the graph representation is explicit and visual (unlike opaque embeddings), engineers can inspect it and find bugs in the retrieval pipeline directly.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I actually already fixed a couple of bugs just thanks to this

takeaways.technique: Build a knowledge graph from semi-structured data first
takeaways.what_they_do: Prioritize semi-structured sources (structured records with long-form text fields) over raw unstructured PDFs, since that's where most enterprise production value is and tooling is more mature.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the middle one is actually where the majority of at least Enterprise production use cases are in the real world
